## Prerequisites:

This documentation presumes the user has some preexisting knowledge of coding in C\# and working with Unity. For a refresher on Unity’s API see [this documentation](https://docs.unity3d.com/2018.4/Documentation/ScriptReference/).

ROUNDS was made in Unity 2018.4.34f1. You will need that version of Unity to be able to make assets for the game, it can be downloaded from [here](https://unity.com/releases/editor/whats-new/2018.4.34).

While not required it is recommended that you install [Visual Studio](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/) making sure to select the .NET desktop development and Unity development components when installing. While you can use any IDE, this is the one I use.  *(If you wish to use Visual Studio Code alongside unity documentation for how to set it up can be found [here](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/other/unity))*

It is also highly recommended that you use [GitHub](https://github.com/) or some other form of version control when working on your mod. It can help keep track of changes if you accidentally break something, and it makes it a lot easier to get help from other developers as they can quickly reference the code base you are working with.

## Setup:

Create a new 3D project in Unity and import [this package](https://drive.google.com/file/d/16XGnC1g0arkZVV7RB5duGw5Qwrxb5muw/view?usp=sharing) into it. The base project contains most common dependencies for ROUNDS mods as well as the base assets that the vanilla cards work, and a template card. *(Take some time to familiarize yourself with the setup of the mod files in Scripts/Mods, their assembly definition files will provide a good reference for any you will have to make.)*

Next make a folder inside of the \`Assets\` folder to hold your mod, you can name it anything you want, but I like to prefix the name with an underscore *(\_)* doing so makes it easier to find as it sorts it to the top of the list.

Inside of that make a folder to hold *all* the code for your mod, and inside of that make a new assembly definition. *(name it the same thing as your mod)* Check the \`override references\` checkbox. This will allow you to reference the game's dll files.   
Under \`assembly definition references\` add \`UnboundLib\` and \`ModdingUtils\`. Then under \`assembly references\` add \`0Harmony.dll\`, \`BepInEx.dll\` and \`Assembly-CSharp.dll\`  
These are the base references that most mods need, if you need to reference additional things they can be added here as well. *(For instructions on how to reference mods not included in the base package, see appendix …)*  
*![][image1]*

## BepInEx Plugin:

Rounds mods use [BepInEx](https://docs.bepinex.dev/) to mod the game. The first step of making a mod is setting up a plugin file. This will be your mod’s entry point into the game.   
Start by making a C\# Script inside the folder that contains your mod’s assembly definition. This is going to be a class file that extends \`BaseUnityPlugin\`. You also need to add the following attributes such that it looks something like this:

| \[BepInDependency("com.willis.rounds.unbound")\]\[BepInDependency("pykess.rounds.plugins.moddingutils")\]\[BepInDependency("pykess.rounds.plugins.cardchoicespawnuniquecardpatch")\]\[BepInPlugin(ModId, ModName, Version)\]\[BepInProcess("Rounds.exe")\]public class MyMod: BaseUnityPlugin{	internal static string modInitials \= "";	void Awake(){			}	void Start(){			}} |
| :---- |

Change \`MyMod\` to be the name of your mod, and replace \`ModId\`, \`ModName\`, and \`Version\` with [appropriate values](https://docs.bepinex.dev/articles/dev_guide/plugin_tutorial/2_plugin_start.html#basic-information-about-the-plugin) *(Version should be a number in the form of \`MajorVersion.MinorVersion.PatchNumber\`)*    
Set modInitials to be the tab you wish for your cards to be regenerated under.

The first 3 lines tell the game that our mod depends on Unbound, ModdingUtils, and CardChoicesSpawnUniqueCardPatch. That means the game will load them first and *not* load our mod if they are not present. It is important to add these lines for any additional mods you end up depending on to ensure that it loads correctly.  
The next line tells BepInEx important information about our mod. The ID is a unique string used for dependence attributes. It should never be changed after releasing your mod.The name should be the human readable name of your mod. The version is what release you are on, how you determine what is a major minor or patch update is up to you, but it is extremely important that you increase this number every time you release an update to the mod, things can break if you don’t as this is how the game ensures everyone is using the same code.  
The final attribute tells BepInEx what game our mod is for, this ensures it won't accidentally be loaded into the wrong game by someone.

The class \`BaseUnityPlugin\` extends MonoBehaviour and will be attached to a gameobject at run time, this means you can use the built-in unity messages such as Awake and Start to set up your mod.

## Making a Card:

In the base package is a template card prefab, copy it into your working directory.   
There are 5 components of interest on the template, Rarity Adder and Theme Adder are used for putting custom rarities and themes on your card and require you to depend on RarityLib and ThemeLib respectively. They should be removed from the template if you do not intend on using those libraries.  
The next component of interest is the CardInfo component:![][image2]  
This is where you set up the visual components of a card

* Card Name is the name that will display for your card.  
* Card Description is the block of text that shows up under the art.  
* Card Stats is an array of card stat objects that are used to generate the displayed stats under the Description.*(change the size value to the number you want to use on your card)*  
  * Positive determines if the stat should be displayed in green or red.  
  * Amount is the coloured part that explains how much a stat is being adjusted by.  
  * Simple Amount will override the Amount field if a player has “Show Card Stat Numbers” disabled.  
  * Stat is the text that explains what is being adjusted.  
* Rarity is a drop down to set the rarity of the card. *(You can only set it to vanilla rarities, This field is ignored if you are using rarity adder)*  
* Card Art can be left as none if you do not want art for your card, or set to a prefab art asset. An explanation of how to make those is [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1w2Qk_n83e3-eAVKZVlYzrT8myphqZspp2VwV7S_DvuA/edit?usp=sharing).  
* Both Sprite and Card Color are not used by the game and can be ignored.  
* Categories is a list of CardCategory objects that are used to tag the card in game. *(They can be created right clicking on the explorer Create \-\> Square Brawl \-\> Card Category)*  
* Allow Multiple will let a player gain more than one copy of a card. *(This is the case for most cards)*  
* Blacklisted Categories is a list of Card Categories that a player will be blocked from getting if they take this card.  
* Card Base is the object that the card is built onto, this can be left alone for now.  
* Color Theme is a drop down to set the theme of the card. *(You can only set it to vanilla theme , This field is ignored if you are using theme adder)*

Finally there are the three components that adjust the players stats: Character Stat Modifiers, Gun, and Block. How these stats work is explained [here](#card-stat-fields:).

Finally you must add the prefab to your asset bundle *(If you haven't made one yet click \`new\` on the drop down menu and type in a name for the bundle IE: \`assets\`)*  
![][image3]  
This will allow you to include it as an asset in your mod’s DLL and load it into the game.

## Building Asset Bundles:

The base unity package included with this documentation includes two scripts to aid in working with asset bundles, both are located in \`Assets\\Editor\`

The first script is \`CreateAssetBundles\` This script adds a button for easy building of the asset bundles, it can be found by clicking Assets and then Build AssetBundles

The second script is \`CsprojPostprocessor\` This script sets up the Csproj file to embed your asset bundle into your mod so it can be used in game. In order to do this you must edit line 9 of the file replacing MODNAME with the name of your mod’s assembly definition, and ASSETBUNDLE with the name of your asset bundle.

| private static Dictionary\<string, string\> ModBundleMap \= new Dictionary\<string, string\>(){   {"MODNAME","ASSETBUNDLE"} *///EDIT WITH NAME OF MOD ASSEMBLY AND NAME OF ASSET BUNDLE (CASE MATTERS)*}; |
| :---- |

Now go back into your main plugin file and add an internal static AssetBundle field named “assets” then in the Awake method add:

| assets \= Jotunn.Utils.AssetUtils.LoadAssetBundleFromResources("ASSETBUNDLE", typeof(MyMod).Assembly); |
| :---- |

replacing \`ASSETBUNDLE\` and \`MyMod\` as necessary. This loads in the asset bundled so you can pull assets out of it later in your mod.

Note: Asset Bundles must be rebuilt when changes are made to their contents in order for the change to actually be reflected in the bundle.

**Important note:** Asset Bundle names are always lowercase and **must** be written as such whenever referenced in code.  
 

## Getting Your Card Into the Game: {#getting-your-card-into-the-game:}

Create a new class to hold and build the cards you are making and copy the following code into it:

| public class CardHolder: MonoBehaviour{    public List\<GameObject\> Cards;    public List\<GameObject\> HiddenCards;    internal void RegisterCards(){        foreach(var Card in Cards){            CustomCard.RegisterUnityCard(Card, MyMod.modInitials, Card.GetComponent\<CardInfo\>().cardName, true, null);        }        foreach(var Card in HiddenCards){            CustomCard.RegisterUnityCard(Card, MyMod.modInitials, Card.GetComponent\<CardInfo\>().cardName, false, null);            ModdingUtils.Utils.Cards.instance.AddHiddenCard(Card.GetComponent\<CardInfo\>());        }    }} |
| :---- |

This class holds 2 lists of cards, Normal cards that you want to show up in a hand, and Hidden cards, which are cards that won’t appear in a player’s hand but can instead be added by other cards.  
The RegisterCards function is a function that you will call in your mod’s main plugin file, it first registers all the normal cards and then registers the hidden cards and flags them as hidden so they can be later accessed.

CustomCard.RegisterUnityCard is a function from unbound for registering cards built inside of unity, it takes 5 parameters 

* The GameObject that holds your card.  
* The Initials of the mod your card is from  
* The CardInfo component on your card  
* Whether or not the card is enabled in CardChoice *(this should be true unless it is a hidden card, then it should be false)*   
* Finally a call back function that takes a CardInfo. This can safely be null if you do not need to use the build callback.

Inside of Unity create a new prefab named \`ModCards\` with the CardHolder component on it and add it to your asset bundle.  
You can now increase the size of the Cards array and add your card to it by dragging and dropping the card prefab onto the cardinfo slot.

You can now tell your mod to register your cards by adding the following line at the end of your Awake method:

| assets.LoadAsset\<GameObject\>("ModCards").GetComponent\<CardHolder\>().RegisterCards(); |
| :---- |

This loads in your CardHolder from the asset bundle and tells it to register all the cards you’ve put in it.

## Compiling and Importing Your Mod:

At this point you should have a mod that adds a simple card to the game, to get it into the game you first have to compile the project into a DLL file, Pressing Ctrl+B inside of Visual Studio will build the project, the output console at the bottom of the will print out a path where the mod has built to. If Visual Studio doesn’t print a path to the location that the dll was built in, look at [Help Visual Studio Isn’t Building My Mod](#help-visual-studio-isn’t-building-my-mod:) for assistance with building it.  
To test your mod, make a new profile in thunderstore or r2modman and install CardChoiceSpawnUniqueCardPatch and any other dependencies your mod might need. Then go to Settings \-\> Profile and select \`Import local mod\`  
![][image4]  
Pick \`Select file\` and then navigate to where your DLL built, pick it, and click \`Select file\`   
You should get a window that looks like this,  
Leave all the fields as they are and click the \`Import local mod\` button.

You should now be able to click \`Start modded\` and have your mod loaded into the game.

## Debugging:

Chances are at some point your mod won't behave as you expect it to. A lot of times when this happens there is an error message sent to the debug log. However, this log is not shown by default. To enable it, select the config editor in your modmanager and select \`Edit Config\` for the \`BepInEx\\Config\\BepInEx.cfg\`. *(You may have to run the game once to make it showup)*   
Then set \`Loging.Console\`  \`Enabled\` to \`true\`. Now the next time you run the game a terminal style debug readout will open with it. Not only will this let you see any errors being thrown, it will also let you add debug lines to your code to aid in debugging. You can do so with the  UnityEngine.Debug.Log(object)  function. Just remember to remove/disable those lines before publishing your mod.  
Another useful tool for debugging is the \`UnityExpolorer\` mod by sinai-dev. This mod lets you look as objects in the game as if they were in the unity editor.

## Porting a Non-Unity Mod Over to Unity:

If you have a mod that you have already created and want to move it over into unity, after following the instructions for setting up your unity project you can copy your mod’s existing code into the code folder you created in unity. Once you do that, provided you have set all necessary references inside the assembly definition, your code should now be accessible inside of unity and all that is left to do is convert your cards over to prefabs.  
First take the [CardHolder](#getting-your-card-into-the-game:) class and modify its RegisterCards function like so:

| internal void RegisterCards(){    foreach(var Card in Cards){        if(Card.GetComponent\<CustomCard\>() is CustomCard customCard){            customCard.BuildUnityCard(null);        }else{            CustomCard.RegisterUnityCard(Card, MyMod.modInitials, Card.GetComponent\<CardInfo\>().cardName, true, null);        }    }    foreach(var Card in HiddenCards){        if(Card.GetComponent\<CustomCard\>() is CustomCard customCard){            customCard.BuildUnityCard(cardInfo \=\> ModdingUtils.Utils.Cards.instance.AddHiddenCard(cardInfo));        }else{            CustomCard.RegisterUnityCard(Card, MyMod.modInitials, Card.GetComponent\<CardInfo\>().cardName, false, null);            ModdingUtils.Utils.Cards.instance.AddHiddenCard(Card.GetComponent\<CardInfo\>());        }    }} |
| :---- |

This will allow you to register cards simply by adding existing CustomCard Monos to prefabs and adding them to your CardHolder like you would do for normal cards, but without the need to set any data on the normal card components.

A convenient way of importing your existing CustomCardMonos is by importing the following script into your unity package.

| using System.IO; using System.Reflection;using UnboundLib.Cards;using UnityEditor;using UnityEngine;using Photon.Pun;public class CreateCustomCardPrefab{    \[MenuItem("Assets/Create/CustomCardPrefab")\]    private static void CreatePrefab()    {        foreach (var obj in Selection.objects)        {            if (obj is MonoScript monoScript)            {                if (monoScript.GetClass().IsSubclassOf(typeof(CustomCard)) && (\!(monoScript.GetClass().GetTypeInfo().IsAbstract)))                {                    GameObject cardObj \= new GameObject(monoScript.GetClass().Name, monoScript.GetClass(), typeof(CardInfo), typeof(PhotonView));                    var customCard \= cardObj.GetComponent\<CustomCard\>();                    customCard.gun \= cardObj.AddComponent\<Gun\>();                    customCard.gun.projectiles \= new ProjectilesToSpawn\[0\];                    customCard.block \= cardObj.AddComponent\<Block\>();                    customCard.statModifiers \= cardObj.AddComponent\<CharacterStatModifiers\>();                    var path \= AssetDatabase.GetAssetPath(obj);                    if (Path.GetExtension(path) \!= "")                    {                        path \= path.Replace(Path.GetFileName(AssetDatabase.GetAssetPath(obj)), "");                    }                    PrefabUtility.SaveAsPrefabAsset(cardObj, $"{path}/{cardObj.name}.prefab");                    GameObject.DestroyImmediate(cardObj);                }            }        }    }    \[MenuItem("Assets/Create/CustomCardPrefab", true)\]    private static bool CreatePrefabValidation()    {        bool flag \= false;        foreach (var obj in Selection.objects)        {            if (obj is MonoScript monoScript)            {                if (monoScript.GetClass().IsSubclassOf(typeof(CustomCard)) && (\!(monoScript.GetClass().GetTypeInfo().IsAbstract)))                {                    flag= true;                }            }        }        return flag;    }} |
| :---- |

This will allow you to simply create a prefab by right-clicking on a monobehaviour script. **Note:** The CustomCard class must have the same name as the file name for this mono to work. 

Finally go into your main plugin file and remove all of the calls to CustomCard.BuildCard as they will all now be handled by the CardHolder. 

*(If you haven't already add the line of code to load and run the CardHolder to your plugin file)*

## Card Stat Fields: {#card-stat-fields:}

Red fields are either not copied off the card, not used by the game, or both.

### Character Stat Modifiers:

| Name | Type | Description | Notes |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Sound Character Slow Freeze | SoundEvent | The sound that is played when a player is slowed down by a slow effect. | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Add Object To Player | GameObject | This is a GameObject that will be added as a child to the player when they get the card |  |
| Size Multiplier | float | Multiplies the current size of the player. | **Never** set this to 0 it will break the game |
| Health | float | Multiplies the max health of the player | **Never** set this to 0 it will break the game |
| Movement Speed | float | Multiplies the movement speed of the player |  |
| Jump | float | Multiplies the jump height of the player |  |
| Gravity | float | Multiplies the force of gravity upon the player | The gravity stat is not reset by default, [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/Root/GravityPatch/) patch fixes that. |
| Slow | float | Used internally for the slow effect | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Slow Slow | float | Used internally for the slow effect | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Fast Slow | float | Used internally for the slow effect | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Seconds To Take Damage Over | float | Increases the amount of time damage is applied to the player over. |  |
| Number Of Jumps | int | Increases the number of jumps the player has | This field will grant infinite jumps without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/Pykess/PlayerJumpPatch/) patch. |
| Regen | float | Causes the player to regenerate that much HP every second | The regen stat is not reset by default, [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/Root/RegenerationPatch/) patch fixes that. |
| Life Steal | float | An additive stat that is multiplied by the amount of damage a player deals to cause them to gain that much life |  |
| Refresh On Damage | bool | If true, the player's attack cooldown will reset when they deal damage.  | Attack cooldown is calculated by their attack speed. |
| Automatic Reload | bool | If set to false, the player will no longer have their gun reload unless it is out of ammo |  |
| Respawns | int | Increases the players number of lives |  |
| Attack Speed Multiplier | float | Used internally by the game for the card Taste Of Blood | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Slow Part | ParticleSystem | The particle effect that is played when a player is slowed down by a slow effect. | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |

### Gun:

| Name | Type | Description | Notes |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Holdable | Holdable | The holdable holding the gun. |  |
| Sound Gun | SoundGun | Produces the gun’s sounds |  |
| Sound Shot Modifier | SoundShotModifier | Modifier for the gun’s sounds. |  |
| Sound Impact Modifier | SoundImpactModifier | Modifiers for the bullet impact sounds. |  |
| Sound Disable Ray Hit Bullet Sound | bool | Disables the impact sounds of bullets when fired. |  |
| Recoil | float | The recoil of the gun when you shoot. |  |
| Body Recoil | float | Additive stat that increases how much recoil force is applied to the player when shooting | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/Root/GunBodyRecoilPatch/) patch. |
| Shake | float | The shake for the gun. |  |
| Force Specific Shake | bool | A flag to set the specific shake of the guns bullets. |  |
| Projectiles | ProjectilesToSpawn\[\] | The bullets that are spawned by the gun. |  |
| Shoot Position | Transform | The transform that gun uses to calculate the direction it shoots in. |  |
| Damage | float  | Multiplies how much damage a player's bullets deal. | This is then multiplied by the projectile's base damage of 55 This is capped at a min of 0.25 This stat is adjusted if the player’s number of projectiles is not 1 and this card’s  number of projectiles is not 0 see ApplyCardStats.CopyGunStats for more details |
| Reload Time | float | Modifies the player's reload time multiplicatively, adjusting the total time including any that was added. |  |
| Reload Time Add | float | Modifies the player's reload time additively, directly adding or removing seconds from it. |  |
| Recoil Muiltiplier | float | Multiplier applied to the Body Recoil stat | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/Root/GunBodyRecoilPatch/) patch. |
| Knockback | float | How much force bullets apply when hitting things. | The force applied also scales with damage. Negative numbers pull the object/player in the direction of the hit, instead of away. |
| Attack Speed | float | The cooldown between attacks. | The name of this stat is very unintuitive as increasing it decreases the rate at which you can attack |
| Projectile Speed | float | How fast the bullet travels. | Referred to as “Bullet Speed” on cards |
| Projectiel Simulaton Speed | float | How fast the bullet travels along its arc of fire. | Referred to as “Projectile Speed” on cards |
| Gravity | float | Modifies the force of gravity on the bullet | If you are setting it to zero *(meaning the bullet will travel in a straight line)* you must depend on [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/TeamDK/ZeroGBulletPatch/) patch |
| Damage After Distance Multiplier | float | Adjusts the damage of the bullet after it moves 10 units. |  |
| Bullet Damage Multiplier | float | How much damage a player's bullets deal. | Unlike Damage the value does not have a minimum, and is not adjusted based on number of projectiles |
| Multiply Spread | float | Multiplies the spread of the bullets. |  |
| Shake M | float | Multiplies the amount the projectile shakes the screen | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Ammo | int | Modifies the amount of ammo a player has for their gun | Game automatically caps to 90 ammo. |
| Ammo Reg | float | Percentage of Ammo regenerated each second. |  |
| Size | float | Modifies the size of the projectile. |  |
| Overheat Multiplier | float | Does not currently do anything in game. |  |
| Time To Reach Full Movement Multiplier | float | Does not currently do anything in game. |  |
| Number Of Projectiles | int | Modifies how many bullets the player shoots each burst. | Setting this to a negative number is dangerous as if it is ever reduced to 0 the player will be unable to shoot |
| Bursts | int | Modifies how many times the player shoots each time they attack. | If the value is less than 1, the player still attacks once. Since 0 is the default value, this means that adding 1 burst results in the same number of attacks.  **Always** use Time Between Bullets in conjunction with Bursts, otherwise you should be using Number Of Projectiles instead. |
| Reflects | int | How many times the bullet bounces off of objects. | Bullets will not bounce off of the void unless you add the ScreenEdgeBounce component to the projectile  |
| Smart Bounce | int | Does not currently do anything in game. |  |
| Bullet Portal | int | Does not currently do anything in game. |  |
| Random Bounces | int | Does not currently do anything in game. |  |
| Time Between Bullets | float | The time between each burst of bullets. | The default value is 0, and you always shoot a minimum of 1 burst of bullets. Meaning that you need to add 2 bursts to see a noticeable effect with one card. |
| Projectile Size | float | Modifies the size of the projectile. | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/Root/GunProjectileSizePatch/) patch. |
| Speed M On Bounce | float | How much the velocity of the bullet changes each time it bounces. |  |
| Dmg M On Bounce | float | How much damage the bullet changes each time it bounces. | If this value is above 1 then the growth it provides will decay by 40% each bounce. |
| Drag | float | How much the bullet is affected by simulated air resistance. |  |
| Drag Min Speed | float | The minimum speed of the bullet when drag is applied to it. | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Spread | float | How far off your bullets are from where you're aiming. | A value of 1 means that bullets can be fired in a full 360 around the player. Negative spread is the same as having positive spread |
| Even Spread | float | How evenly bullets are distributed among the bullets arc of spread. | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/willuwontu/EvenSpreadPatch/) patch. |
| Percentage Damage | float | How much of the target's max HP adds as additional damage. | A value of 1 means that bullets deal 100% of the target's HP. |
| Cos | float | The amplitude of the bullet’s sinusoidal movement. |  |
| Slow | float | How much the target is slowed when hit | Each hit stacks with the previous slow on the target, causing multiple bullets to slow the target exponentially. |
| Charge Damage Multiplier | float | How much the bullet’s damage is multiplied by the current charge when it is fired. | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/willuwontu/GunChargePatch/) patch. |
| Charge Spread To | float | How much the gun’s spread is affected by its current charge. | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/willuwontu/GunChargePatch/) patch. |
| Charge Even Spread To | float | How much the gun’s even spread is affected by its current charge. | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/willuwontu/GunChargePatch/) patch. |
| Charge Speed To | float | How much the bullet’s speed is multiplied by the current charge of the gun when it is fired. | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/willuwontu/GunChargePatch/) patch. |
| Charge Recoil To | float | If the gun is using charge, will multiply the Body Recoil stat by this times the guns current charge when shooting | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/Root/GunBodyRecoilPatch/) patch and [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/willuwontu/GunChargePatch/) patch. |
| Charge Number Of Projectiles To | float | How many additional projectiles the gun will fire at max charge. | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/willuwontu/GunChargePatch/) patch. Default value is 0\. |
| Destroy Bullet After | float | The amount of time a bullet lives for after it’s  |  |
| Force Specific Attack Speed | float | The forced attack speed of the gun. | Only works if Lock Gun To Default is set to true. |
| Lock Gun To Default | bool | Forces the gun to shoot at a specific attack speed with no spread, and only fires 1 bullet at a time. |  |
| Unblockable | bool | Flag that enables the bullets to deal damage through shields. | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/Pykess/GunUnblockablePatch/h/) patch. |
| Ignore Walls | bool | Flag that enables the bullets to go through walls. |  |
| Use Charge | bool | Causes the gun to use a charge system for firing. None of the charge fields work properly without this being set to true. | This field will have no effect without [this](https://rounds.thunderstore.io/package/willuwontu/GunChargePatch/) patch. |
| Dont Allow Auto Fire | bool | Prevents a player from firing their gun by holding down the shoot button. |  |
| Objects To Spawn | ObjectsToSpawn\[\] | Objects that are attached to the bullet to provide additional effects and capabilities. | Explanation of the ObjectsToSpawn object [here](#objectstospawn:) |
| Projectile Color | Color | The colour of the bullet. |  |
| Wave Movement | bool | Does not currently do anything in game | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Teleport | bool | Does not currently do anything in game | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Spawn Skelleton Square | bool | Does not currently do anything in game | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Explode Near Enemy Range | float | Does not currently do anything in game | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Explode Near Enemy Damage | float | Does not currently do anything in game | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Hit Movement Multiplier | float | Does not currently do anything in game | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |
| Attack Speed Multiplier | float | Set every frame via CharacterStatModifiers. | This is not copied off of cards so setting it will have no effect. |

### Block:

| Name | Type | Description | Notes |

## 

## On Add/On Remove Effects:

If you want to have some kind of effect applied/removed from a player when they take/lose a card you can use the Add Object To Player field on the Character Stat Modifiers to add a gameobject with a mono-behavior on it to the player. The game will automatically remove the object if the player loses the card.  
The void Start(){} function is called when the card is added, and the void OnDestroy(){} function is called when the card is removed. To get the player the card is on, simply call GetComponentInParent\<Player\>()

## 

## Reversible Effects:

Sometimes you need to apply a temporary stat change to a player. This should be done using the ReversibleEffect class from ModdingUtils to ensure that it plays nicely with other temporary stat changes. It should also **never** be active during the pick phase or it could have permanent side effects. To use a reversible effect, create a new class that extends the base ReversibleEffect class and then set any necessary values for stat changes in either the OnAwake or OnStart functions. The stat changes are stored to the variables \`gunStatModifier\`, \`gunAmmoStatModifier\`, \`characterDataModifier\`, characterStatModifierModifier\`, \`gravityModifier\`, \`blockModifier\`, and \`healthHandlerModifier\`.   
For each stat that the modifiers can modify there is an “add” stat and a  “mult” stat, for example \`HealthHandlerModifier\` has \`regen\_add\` which when applied adds its value to the regen stat, and \`regen\_mult\` which when applied multiples the regen stat by its value. There are too many variables to list out here, however, if you would like to look at the extensive list, all of the stat change modifiers exist in [this](https://github.com/pdcook/ModdingUtils/blob/5d014e8c0951c55de972ec98d52f19270fff6505/ModdingUtils/Extensions/TemporaryModifiers.cs) file.  
Once you set up the stats you wish to adjust, set the \`livesToEffect\` to the number of lives that the effect should apply for. The effects will apply automatically at the end of the start function, if you need to add a delay to that, set \`applyImmediately\` to false. When the component is destroyed the effects will be removed, however, if you need to have logic turning the effect on and off, that can be done by calling the \`ApplyModifers\` and ClearModifiers\` functions respectively.

## Syncing Random Numbers and Other Things:

Everything in rounds is handled client-sided; this means that if you need something to happen based on a random number, *(For example an ability that only has a 25% chance to go off)*  then you need to run the calculation on only a single client, and then sync the outcome to every other client.   
First you need to determine which client you wish to run the calculation on, there are two options for this, the client the of the user that the rng is tide to, this is normally what is done when the effect effects a single specific player, or the master client, which is typically used for all other effects. If you wish to run the calculation on the master client, check the value of \`PhotonNetwork.IsMasterClient\`  it will be true only if the code is being run on the master client. Otherwise, if you have a specific player you can check \`player.data.view.isMine\` which will only be true on that player’s computer.   
Once you have determined the outcome of the random event, you must inform the other clients using an RPC (Remote Procedure Call) which is a fancy type of function that allows code to be called from one client to another. Unbound adds utilities to make making and using RPCs easier. Using unbound, RPCs are static functions that return void and take only primitive types as parameters *(primitive types are the basic types in a language, such as int, string, or bool)* and are annotated with \`\[UnboundRPC\]\`. Inside of that function is where you would put all of the code that needs to be run on all clients, such as stat adjustments. To call the RPC, run  \`NetworkingManager.RPC\` this will tell every client to run the RPC, it takes the following parameters:

* The **Type** of the class that the RPC is defined on. *(The typeof function can be used to obtain the needed type)*  
* A **string** that is the name of the RPC function. *(The nameof function can be used here to avoid having to change the name in multiple places if you refactor what the RPC is called)*  
*  Finally add the values of each parameter of the RPC you are calling as separate parameters. *(If you wish they can also be passed in a single **object\[\]**)*

You can also use \`NetworkingManager.RPC\_Others\` using the same parameters and it will run the code on every client other then the one that called it. Do note though, that calling this function in offline mode *(local play)* will cause it to run the RPC anyways so you should always make sure that \`PhotonNetwork.OfflineMode\` is false before running RPC\_Others.

## **Help Visual Studio Isn’t Building My Mod**: {#help-visual-studio-isn’t-building-my-mod:}

For some reason, the visual studio unity plugin has a setting that by default will stop it from properly building to DLLs.This can be turned off by selecting the \`Tools\` drop down, then select \`Options\`.  
Inside of the menu this opens, pick \`Tools for Unity\` then \`General\` and under the \`Miscellaneous\` header, set \`Disable the full build of projects\` to \`**False**\` 

## Tips/Tricks:

### Extending CardInfo:

One convenient way to store additional information on your cards is to extend the CardInfo component and add extra fields to it, then use that on your prefabs instead of the normal one you will still have access to the original CardInfo fields and as long as you don't override the Awake function it will continue to work in game with no other code.

### Using In-game Volume for Audio:

When adding sound effects to the game, they should be added using a \`SoundUnityEventPlayer\` component. Then you can add the \`AudioMixerFixer\` component from ModdingUtils to the same gameobject and it will let you set which of the 3 in-game volume sliders to tie the volume of your sound to.

### Automatic Namespaces:

The option to have unity automatically generate namespaces for your files was not introduced until unity 2019 which sadly is a major version after the one we need to use for rounds. However, having namespaces is an important feature of coding as it helps keep code organized between mods. Because of this, I created an editor script to automatically add Namespaces to my files when I created them. I will share the code here, however do note that it only works if you follow the folder structure that I use *(Having your main project folder named \`\_\_ProjectName\` and then having your code directly in that folder or in a subfolder named \`Code\` you can then use subfolders inside of your parent code folder to make sub-namespaces)* 

| using System.Collections.Generic;using System.IO;using System.Linq;public class NamespaceGenerator:UnityEditor.AssetModificationProcessor {	static void OnWillCreateAsset(string assetName) {        	    	UnityEngine.Debug.Log(assetName);        	    	if(\!assetName.EndsWith("cs.meta")) return;        	    	UnityEngine.Debug.Log("Updating " \+ assetName.Substring(0, assetName.Length \- 5));        	    	List\<string\> newFile \= new List\<string\>();        	    	bool added \= false;        	    	string NameSpace \= "";        	    	bool found \= false;        	    	int count \= assetName.Count(f \=\> f \== '/') \- 1;        	    	int replaced \= 0;        	    	string fileName \= assetName;        	    	if(fileName.Contains("/code/")) {        	        	        	var temp \= "";         	        	        	for(int i \= 0; i \< fileName.Length; i++) {        	            	        	        	temp+= fileName\[i\];        	            	        	        	if(temp.Contains("/code/")) {        	                	        	        	fileName \= fileName.Substring(i \+ 1);        	                	        	        	found \= true;        	            	        	        	}        	        	        	}        	    	}        	    	foreach(char c in fileName) {        	        	        	if(c \== '\_') found=true;        	        	        	if(found && c \!= '\_')        	            	        	        	if(c \== '/' && \++replaced \< count)        	                	        	        	NameSpace \+= ".";        	                    		else if(replaced \== count)        	                	        	        	break;        	            	        	        	else NameSpace \+= c;        	    	}        	    	StreamReader sr \= new StreamReader(assetName.Substring(0, assetName.Length\-5));        	    	for(string line \= sr.ReadLine(); line \!= null; line \= sr.ReadLine()) {        	        	        	if(line.Contains("class") && \!added) {        	            	        	        	newFile.Add("namespace " \+ NameSpace \+ " {");        	            	        	        	added \= true;        	        	        	}        	        	        	if(added) newFile.Add('\\t' \+ line);        	        	        	else newFile.Add(line);        	    	}        	    	newFile.Add("}");        	    	sr.Close();        	    	StreamWriter sw \= new StreamWriter(assetName.Substring(0, assetName.Length \- 5),false);        	    	newFile.ForEach(f \=\> sw.WriteLine(f));        	    	sw.Close();	}} |
| :---- |

Putting this in your project’s \`Editor\` folder to edit any **New** cs scripts created to have a namespace set.
